original_title: CStone secures China IND approval for EGFR/HER3 bispecific ADC CS5007 - BioSpectrum Asia
title: CStone's EGFR/HER3 bispecific ADC gets the IND nod in China
blurb: CS5007, a bispecific ADC hitting both EGFR and HER3, cleared IND approval in China. Standard bispecific ADC logic, one conjugate covering two receptors.

original_title: Supply Chain Execution in Radiopharma: The Industry’s Next Critical Challenge - BioPharm International
title: The radiopharma bottleneck nobody's marketing: logistics
blurb: A trade piece arguing that supply chain execution, getting short-half-life radiopharmaceuticals from production to patient before they decay, is shaping up as the industry's next big operational headache.

original_title: CSPC Advances Chemo-Free ADC Combo In 1L NSCLC - insights.citeline.com
title: CSPC pushes a chemo-free ADC combo into first-line NSCLC
blurb: CSPC is advancing a combination of ADCs, no chemotherapy, as a first-line non-small-cell lung cancer regimen. Part of the broader push to get ADCs into frontline slots chemo has held for decades.

original_title: CsPbBr3 Enabled Skeletal Divergence of N-Arylglycine via Deoxygenative Spiroannulation
title: Perovskite nanocrystals redirect glycine chemistry toward new spirooxindoles
blurb: CsPbBr3 nanocrystals under visible light drive a deoxygenative spirocyclization of isatins with N-arylglycines, building spiro-imidazolidine oxindoles in one step. The point is the divergence: N-arylglycines usually run down a well-worn annulation path, and this reroutes them to a different skeletal scaffold entirely.

original_title: Hydrogels based on vinyl amino acids: from preparation to biomedical applications
title: A review of hydrogels built from vinyl amino acids
blurb: Rounds up how vinyl amino acid hydrogels get made, what they can do, and where they're used in biomedicine, plus the usual list of open challenges. A review, so a map of the field rather than a new result.

original_title: Open-chain and cyclic nitrenium ions: generation, characterization, structure and (bio)chemical reactivity
title: A review of nitrenium ions, open-chain and cyclic
blurb: Covers how nitrenium ions get generated, their electronic structure and reactivity, and their role in catalysis and biochemistry, both open-chain and cyclic forms. Reference material rather than a new finding.

original_title: Computational mechanisms of spin-influenced organic reactions catalyzed by 3d iron-group metals
title: How spin state quietly runs iron-group catalysis
blurb: A computational review tracking C–H activation and alkene chemistry on mono- and binuclear 3d iron-group metal complexes, where the mechanism only makes sense once you follow the spin state along the way. It's a review, so no new reactions, just the theory tying the observed weirdness together.

original_title: Enzymatic double crosslinking strategy: remodeling of pea protein isolate hydrogels through transglutaminase and gelatin modification to redesign their functional properties.
title: Two enzymes crosslink pea protein into better hydrogels
blurb: Transglutaminase plus modified gelatin double-crosslink pea protein isolate into hydrogels, aimed at tuning texture and function for food use. Published in Food Research International, so read it as food science, not biomedical.

original_title: A Phase-3, Open-Label, Randomized Study of Dato-DXd Versus Investigator's Choice of Chemotherapy (ICC) in Participants With Inoperable or Metastatic HR-Positive, HER2-Negative Breast Cancer Who Have Been Treated With One or Two Prior Lines of Systemic Chemotherapy (TROPION-Breast01)
title: AstraZeneca's ADC goes head-to-head with chemo again
blurb: Phase 3 trial pitting Dato-DXd against investigator's-choice chemo, capecitabine included, in HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer patients already through one or two prior chemo lines. It's active but not recruiting, so this is one to watch for a readout rather than to sign up for.

original_title: Outcomes of [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 radioligand therapy with and without concurrent enzalutamide in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer: a single-center retrospective study
title: Does adding enzalutamide help PSMA radioligand therapy
blurb: A single-center retrospective comparing Lu-177-PSMA-617 outcomes with and without concurrent enzalutamide in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Single-center and retrospective, so it's a lead for a proper trial design, not an answer.
venue: European Journal of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging

original_title: Affinity enhancement of polo-like kinase 1 polo-box domain-binding peptides by N -methylation and lipidation
title: Lipidation beats methylation for gluing peptides to Plk1
blurb: N-methylating Plk1 polo-box domain binding peptides bought up to 4-fold better affinity, lipidating the same parent peptide bought up to 260-fold. One of these tweaks is doing almost all the work.

original_title: BWXT Selling Medical Business to Nordic Capital in Transaction Valued at up to $800 Million - Business Wire
title: BWXT cashes out of the medical isotope business
blurb: BWXT is selling its medical unit to Nordic Capital for up to $800 million. Not a science result, but worth noting when it's about who ends up owning isotope production and radiopharma supply.

original_title: An evaluation of becotatug vedotin for the treatment of recurrent or metastatic nasopharyngeal cancer.
title: A checkup on becotatug vedotin for nasopharyngeal cancer
blurb: An expert opinion piece assessing where the ADC becotatug vedotin stands for recurrent or metastatic nasopharyngeal cancer. Thin on specifics, so treat it as a status summary rather than new trial data.

original_title: The Ugi–Joullié three-component reaction (UJ-3CR) and related reactions: recent developments, mechanistic aspects and synthesis of natural products and bioactive compounds
title: The Ugi reaction's quieter three-component cousin
blurb: A review of the Ugi–Joullié three-component reaction, which builds polysubstituted nitrogen heterocycles from cyclic imines, isonitriles, and carboxylic acids, covering its mechanism and use in natural product synthesis. Handy as a reference for what the scaffold can build, not a new result itself.

original_title: Iridium-Catalyzed Enantioselective Nucleophilic Coupling of Sulfoxonium Ylides with Ylide Retention
title: Sulfoxonium ylides finally get to act as nucleophiles instead of leaving groups
blurb: An iridium-catalyzed allylic substitution uses sulfoxonium ylides as carbon nucleophiles for the first time while keeping the ylide moiety intact, building stereocenters with high branched selectivity and up to >99% ee. The retention is the trick here, since most ylide chemistry burns the ylide up as it reacts.

original_title: Room-temperature synthesis of crystalline one-dimensional covalent organic frameworks
title: Crystalline 1D COFs without the usual heat
blurb: One-dimensional covalent organic frameworks made crystalline at room temperature, with n-butanol standing in for the solvothermal conditions this chemistry usually needs.

original_title: P‐Directed and Lewis Acid‐Assisted Pd‐Catalyzed Si─Me Bond Activation Enabling Alkyl Exchange at Silicon
title: Getting palladium to actually touch a Si–Me bond
blurb: Si–Me bonds are strong and low-polarity enough that Pd usually ignores them. Here a P-directing group plus a Pd catalyst plus a Lewis acid gets it done: DFT says the Lewis acid yanks off a methide and that triggers a cationic silyl-Pd complex that carries out the alkyl exchange at silicon. They ran it through a four-step sequence to show it's actually useful for editing Si substituents stepwise, not just a stoichiometric curiosity.

original_title: Platinum-Catalyzed C3 - Ipso Deep C–F Editing of Allylic Gem -Difluorides via Base-Switchable Divergent Annulation
title: Two C–F bonds traded for a ring, and the base decides which ring
blurb: A Pt(0)-catalyzed reaction takes allylic gem-difluorides and o-indolyl phenols and swaps out both C–F bonds to stitch together indole-fused O-heterocycles, something Pt-catalyzed allylic chemistry hasn't done well before. Base-free conditions send it through C,O-annulation off the indole C3 position, switch to NaH and the pathway diverges toward nitrogen instead. One substrate, one switch, two ring systems.

original_title: Rapidly photocleavable triazene-functionalized nucleotides for DNA sequencing
title: A quicker light switch for sequencing nucleotides
blurb: Triazene-tagged nucleotides built to photocleave fast, aimed at DNA sequencing chemistry where the deprotection step is usually the bottleneck.

original_title: Recent advances in the total synthesis of coumarin-based natural products
title: A field guide to building coumarins the hard way
blurb: A review rounding up recent total syntheses of coumarin natural products, focused on the catalytic and biomimetic tricks people are using to shorten routes and deal with the coumarin core's usual construction headaches. No new chemistry here, just the state of the art laid out.

original_title: Noninnocent Deep Eutectic Solvents Enable Selective, Sustainable Nickel‐Catalyzed Cross‐Electrophile Couplings to Diarylmethanes
title: Cross-electrophile coupling without the nasty amide solvent
blurb: Aryl iodides and benzyl chlorides coupled to diarylmethanes with a Ni catalyst, but run in a choline chloride/urea deep eutectic solvent instead of the usual hazardous amides. Mild, aerobic, heterogeneous, zinc as the reductant, up to 95% yield with wide functional group tolerance. First time this coupling's been done that sustainably, per the authors.

original_title: Organomediator enabled electrochemically regioselective 1,2-arylalkylation of alkenes with aryl and alkyl halides
title: Electrochemistry does the alkene arylalkylation, no metal needed
blurb: An organomediator drives a regioselective 1,2-arylalkylation of alkenes with aryl and alkyl halides under electrochemical conditions, mild and broad scope, with no noble-metal catalyst in sight. Used here to make 1,1-diarylalkanes.

original_title: Designing biomimetic hydrogels for neuro-therapeutic delivery devices for brain soft tissue injury: integrating antioxidant, cell viability and tissue adhesion properties to enhance neural regeneration via a synergistic approach
title: A hydrogel built to sit at the site of a nerve injury
blurb: Carrageenan copolymerized with a zwitterionic polymer into a network hydrogel meant to deliver drugs right at nerve damage while also acting as antioxidant, staying cell-friendly, and sticking to the tissue. A lot of boxes checked at once, which is exactly the kind of claim worth watching for follow-up beyond the bench.

original_title: Construction of a chitosan/γ-poly(glutamic acid) composite hydrogel crosslinked by ZIF-8 for enhanced α-glucosidase immobilization and inhibitor screening.
title: A MOF-crosslinked hydrogel for parking an enzyme
blurb: Chitosan and γ-poly(glutamic acid) crosslinked with the MOF ZIF-8 into a composite hydrogel, built to immobilize α-glucosidase so it can be reused for inhibitor screening.

original_title: Innovative mechanochemical synthesis of lipopeptide surfactants through direct amidation of fatty esters: application to silk-derived amphiphilic lipopeptides
title: Ball-milling fatty esters straight into lipopeptide surfactants
blurb: A mechanochemical route makes lipoamino acids by direct amidation of fatty esters, skipping the usual solvent-heavy amidation. They then used it to build amphiphilic lipopeptides out of silk sericin.

original_title: Clinical translation and landscape of stimuli-responsive nanomedicines and microscale therapeutics
title: Counting how many stimuli-responsive nanomedicines actually make it to clinic
blurb: A scientometric sweep of stimuli-responsive nano- and microscale therapeutics across preclinical and clinical stages, mapping where the translation pipeline actually breaks down and what's been proposed to fix it. A landscape paper, not a new therapy, so the real content is in the barriers it maps out.

original_title: Design and organocatalytic enantioselective assembly of axially chiral boracyclohexylidenes and chiral boraspiranes
title: Building axial chirality straight onto boron
blurb: An organocatalytic route to axially chiral boracyclohexylidenes and boraspiranes, putting the chirality on boron-containing rings instead of the usual carbon scaffolds. The snippet is bare bones, but boron-centered axial chirality is still a rare enough design target to flag.

original_title: Photoredox/Nickel-Catalyzed Decarboxylative Monofluoromethylation of β-Boryl NHPI Esters via Radical 1,2-Boron Migration
title: A boron shuffle clears the way for a fluoromethyl group
blurb: Photoredox and nickel working in tandem to push a 1,2-boron migration: a β-boryl NHPI ester loses CO2, the boron slides over, and the resulting carbon radical gets coupled to a monofluoromethyl radical. End product is a congested quaternary carbon still carrying a usable boronate, with broad scope and decent functional group tolerance to go with it.

original_title: Direct Molecular Editing of Complex Molecules for Drug Discovery
title: A field map for editing molecules instead of building them from scratch
blurb: A review sorting the growing pile of molecular editing methods, mostly aimed at natural products and drugs, into skeletal edits (swapping atoms in the ring) and peripheral edits (swapping what hangs off it). No new chemistry here, just a rundown of where late-stage diversification methods currently stand.

original_title: Co-thermal coupling of carbonate decomposition and propane dehydrogenation via hydrogen transfer
title: Making one endothermic reaction pay for another's heat bill
blurb: Propane dehydrogenation generates hydrogen as it runs, and this setup feeds that hydrogen straight into carbonate decomposition, so the two equilibrium-limited reactions offset each other instead of both demanding brutal temperatures separately. Calcium carbonate's decomposition point drops meaningfully as a result, which matters given how much energy these processes normally burn just staying hot enough to proceed.

original_title: Sustainable stability-indicating spectra manipulations for the concurrent quantification of gliclazide and its impurity A as the possible alkaline degradation product: Multi-Color Analytical Profile Assessment
title: Watching gliclazide degrade without ever separating it from what it degrades into
blurb: First-derivative spectrophotometry plus Fourier self-deconvolution pulls gliclazide and its alkaline degradation impurity apart on the raw UV spectrum, no chromatography needed, linear from 2.5-25 µg/mL for the drug and 2.5-15 for the impurity. The whole pitch is a stability-indicating assay that skips separation entirely.

original_title: Continuous flow reductive amination of cyclohexanone using Pd/C catalyst with high productivity
title: Cyclohexanone to its dimethylamine, in flow, over Pd/C
blurb: A continuous-flow reductive amination of cyclohexanone tuned for high yield and productivity, delivering N,N-dimethylcyclohexanamine. Unglamorous chemistry, just a flow process claiming to outrun the batch version.

original_title: A tetrazine-driven photocatalytic system suitable for the synthesis of unstable 2,3-dihydroisoxazoles
title: A tetrazine dye lets visible light build the isoxazolines that don't usually survive synthesis
blurb: A pytz-catalyzed [3+2] cycloaddition between nitrones and alkynyl esters, run under visible light, reaches 2,3-dihydroisoxazoles described as too unstable to access cleanly by other routes.

original_title: Water-compatible acylation reactions with acid chlorides using a flow microreactor
title: Getting acid chlorides to behave in water, as long as it's flow
blurb: A flow microreactor runs acylations with acid chlorides directly in aqueous medium and still beats hydrolysis, hitting 98% yield at 2.1 g/h on drug-relevant substrates. The trick is presumably just keeping residence time short enough that water doesn't win the race.

original_title: Visible light-induced ipso -chalcogenation of aryl/alkenyl boronic acids assisted by a chalcogen-radical transfer (ChRT) strategy
title: Trading a boronic acid for sulfur, selenium, or tellurium under visible light
blurb: A fully organophotocatalytic, visible-light ipso-chalcogenation swaps the boronic acid group on aryl and alkenyl boronic acids for a chalcogen radical, giving unsymmetrical diaryl sulfides, selenides, and tellurides in one step, metal-free.

original_title: Thermodynamic hydration boundaries guide storage and closed-loop recycling of sodium-ion battery cathodes
title: Mapping the exact moment a sodium-ion cathode starts drinking water
blurb: Alluaudite sodium iron sulfate is a cheap, high-voltage sodium-ion cathode that's a pain around humidity. This maps the temperature and water-vapor-pressure boundaries separating its anhydrous, hydrated, and deliquesced states, then turns that same moisture sensitivity into a closed-loop recycling process. The handling problem becomes the recycling method.

original_title: Direct electrosynthesis of aromatic nitriles from methylarenes with hydroxylamine as a nitrogen source
title: Turning a methylarene straight into a nitrile with electricity
blurb: An electrochemical route that converts a methyl group on an arene directly to a nitrile, using hydroxylamine as the nitrogen source, under conditions billed as mild and sustainable rather than the usual stoichiometric oxidant slog.

original_title: NF 3 for difluoroamination of tertiary lithium reagents
title: NF3, usually an etchant gas, doing double duty as an -NF2 source
blurb: Organolithium reagents reduce nitrogen trifluoride by a single electron, and the resulting species hands off an -NF2 group onto a tertiary carbon. A genuinely different way to get difluoroamines, though NF3 is not a reagent most benches keep lying around.

original_title: Diversity‐Oriented Two‐Step Annulative π‐Extension Enables Access to Structurally Complex Nanographenes
title: APEX nanographene synthesis gets an actual reagent menu
blurb: Annulative pi-extension usually caps out on whatever aromatic ring the one available reagent lets you bolt on. This splits the process into two steps built around naphthalene-based aryltrimethylsilanes, which lets structurally diverse PAHs and nanographenes come out the other end instead of one fixed shape.

original_title: Diastereoselective intramolecular O -allylation with alkynes using palladium/Brønsted acid combined catalysis: access to substituted chiral oxazolidines
title: Alkynes as the allyl source for chiral oxazolidines, no waste
blurb: A palladium/Brønsted acid tandem catalyzes intramolecular O-allylation directly off an alkyne, fully atom-economical, turning cheap starting material into vinyl-substituted chiral oxazolidines with good diastereoselectivity.

original_title: Metal-free synthesis of highly substituted 2-aminopyridines by formal [3+3] annulation of α,α-dicyanoalkenes with imines
title: 2-Aminopyridines built with zero metal catalyst
blurb: A formal [3+3] annulation between alpha,alpha-dicyanoalkenes and N-cyanoimines assembles substituted 2-aminopyridines metal-free, with broad functional group tolerance.

original_title: Inside Front Cover: Water, Alcohols, Amines, and Amides as Formal Hydrogen‐Atom‐Transfer Reagents Through Activation With Redox‐Active Lewis Acids
title: Water and amines pressed into service as hydrogen-atom donors
blurb: Redox-active Lewis acids activate ordinary water, alcohols, amines, and amides so they can act as formal hydrogen-atom-transfer reagents, standing in for the usual thiol or silane hydride sources.

original_title: Structural engineering of Pd/C catalyst for selective hydrogenation of bulky quinone to biphenol
title: Getting Pd nanoparticle size right cleans up a stubborn quinone hydrogenation
blurb: Dispersing Pd/C down to ~4.1 nm nanoparticles hydrogenates the bulky quinone TBDPQ to TBBP at 98.5% conversion and 99.0% selectivity, at a fairly mild 100°C and 3 MPa H2. Bulky quinones are usually where selective hydrogenation falls apart, so that selectivity number is the actual result.

original_title: Alcoholysis of nylon 6 waste to ε-caprolactam promoted by phosphoric acid
title: Phosphoric acid breaks nylon 6 waste back down to its monomer
blurb: Phosphoric acid promotes alcoholysis of nylon 6 waste back to epsilon-caprolactam, recovering the actual monomer rather than just downcycling the plastic into something lesser.

original_title: Electrochemical Robustness and Spin-Selective Transport in Self-Assembled MYG-0 Peptide Monolayers
title: A peptide monolayer that filters spin and survives doing it
blurb: Self-assembled MYG-0 peptide monolayers on gold show chiral-induced spin selectivity, and conductive AFM confirms the film forms as a clean, continuous layer. The usual problem with these devices isn't the spin filtering, it's holding up electrochemically under real fields, which is the part being claimed here.

original_title: Palladium-catalyzed migratory allylic sulfonylation of allylic alcohols using sulfonyl hydrazides
title: Sulfonyl hydrazides do a migratory allylic sulfonylation under Pd catalysis
blurb: Palladium catalysis shuttles a sulfonyl group onto a new position of an allylic alcohol using sulfonyl hydrazides as the sulfonyl source, with good chemo- and regioselectivity.

original_title: Understanding the Role of the Local Structure Optimization in Cu–S-Based Single-Atom Catalysts for Oxygen Electroreduction
title: Tuning how far the sulfur sits from copper changes ORR activity
blurb: Three Cu-S single-atom catalysts, same metal, sulfur parked at different distances from the Cu center, built to pin down which coordination geometry actually drives oxygen reduction. Useful mechanistic groundwork for fuel cells and metal-air batteries, though it's still single-atom catalyst tinkering rather than a working electrode.

original_title: A self-floating, water lily-inspired artificial leaf for photocatalytic hydrogen peroxide production from water, air, and sunlight across the tri-phase interface
title: A floating artificial leaf that makes its own hydrogen peroxide
blurb: Cellulose plays mesophyll, a covalent organic framework plays chloroplast, and the whole assembly floats on water to make H2O2 straight from sunlight, water, and air at the tri-phase interface. Cute biomimicry, but it's a lab-scale leaf, not a peroxide plant.

original_title: Synergistic Surface and Interface Regulation of Ultralow-Pt-Loading Cathodes for Low-Alkalinity AEMWEs
title: Keeping Pt cathodes alive when the alkalinity gets stingy
blurb: Anion exchange membrane electrolyzers want to run at low alkalinity to cut costs, but that starves the cathode kinetically and chokes interfacial transport. Pairing ultralow Pt/C loading with a melamine-isophthalic acid hydrogen-bonded organic framework reworks both the surface and the interface to hold performance under those harsher conditions.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Accelerated HER kinetics via electron-deficient Ni and electron-enriched Se sites by dual Fe and Mn doping for highly efficient hydrogen production
title: Doping both metal and chalcogen sites to speed up hydrogen evolution
blurb: Fe and Mn co-doping into Ni0.85Se on nickel foam pulls electron density off the Ni sites and pushes it onto Se, and that push-pull lowers the HER energy barrier. At least the synthesis is unglamorous: electrodeposit, then selenize.

original_title: Hydrogen bond regulation to enhance catalytic C–C bond cleavage of polylactic acid wastes in H 2 O to produce H 2
title: Turning PLA plastic waste into hydrogen, nearly all of it
blurb: A Ni-Fe catalyst plus a hydrogen bond regulation trick cleaves the C-C bonds in polylactic acid waste sitting in water, pushing the breakdown almost entirely to CO2 and H2. Waste-to-hydrogen papers are common; the near-complete conversion claim is the part worth checking against messier feedstocks than clean PLA.

original_title: Interfacial polarization enables dual pathways for electrosynthesis of propyl acetate
title: One Cu/Cu3N interface, two coupling pathways, one ester
blurb: Charge polarization at a Cu/Cu3N interface drives both C-C and C-O coupling at once during CO electroreduction, funneling the reaction selectively toward propyl acetate instead of the usual grab-bag of C2+ products. A five-carbon ester as a selective target out of CO electrolysis is an unusual thing to land on.

original_title: Flexible graphene paper for large-scale electroorganic synthesis: C–H amination of benzoxazole derivatives
title: A graphene paper electrode built for scaling up electrosynthesis
blurb: Flexible graphene paper serves as the electrode for large-batch electrochemical C-H amination of benzoxazole derivatives, chasing the usual electrosynthesis pitch of milder reagents and less waste. The paper electrode format is the actual selling point here, not the amination chemistry itself.

original_title: Photophysics of click-functionalized 2,2′-bithienyl flexible Lewis pairs
title: Flexible Lewis pairs that change color with temperature and solvent
blurb: Bithienyl-based frustrated Lewis pairs get a click-chemistry makeover, and the resulting flexible pairs show absorption and emission that shift with both temperature and solvent, evidence the pair's open/closed equilibrium actually responds to its environment. Pure photophysics groundwork, no application claimed.

original_title: Switchable and biodegradable nanostructures for safe and precise tumor diagnostics
title: A design manual for nanostructures that turn on, then get out
blurb: A tutorial review, not new data, laying out design rules for switchable, biodegradable nanoparticles in cancer imaging: activate specifically at the tumor, stay stable en route, clear the body afterward. Useful if you're building one of these, skippable if you wanted new results.

original_title: KBr-enabled electrochemical transformation of alkynes into α-bromoketones/1,2-diketones
title: KBr doing double duty in an alkyne-to-diketone electrosynthesis
blurb: One cheap salt, two jobs: KBr supplies both the bromine and the supporting electrolyte in an electrochemical route from alkynes to alpha-bromoketones or 1,2-diketones. Which product you get presumably comes down to conditions, worth checking before assuming you can dial it at will.

original_title: π-Spacer effects in 2,6-disubstituted BODIPY fluorophores for mitochondrial imaging
title: Tuning the π-spacer to get BODIPY dyes into mitochondria
blurb: Swapping the π-spacer between the BODIPY core and its organelle-targeting motif shifts both the optical properties and how well the dye actually images mitochondria. Standard structure-property crawl, but useful if you're picking a scaffold for live-cell imaging.

original_title: A Thirty-Year Gap: Reviving All-Nitride Glasses as Processable, High-Performance Materials
title: Reviving a glass nobody could make for 30 years
blurb: All-nitride glasses got reported once in the 90s by Grande, Holloway, McMillan and Angell, then sat unreplicated because the synthesis conditions were brutal. This revisits them now that the equipment problem is gone, betting oxygen-free nitride glasses can do what conventional glass systems are stuck on. Whether the performance actually clears that bar is the open part.

original_title: Synthesis and evaluation of carbagalactosyl 1,2-aziridines and -epoxides as glycosidase inhibitors
title: Galacto-cyclophellitol aziridines hit beta- but not alpha-galactosidases
blurb: These 1,2-galacto-configured cyclophellitol aziridines covalently knock out β-galactosidases but leave the alpha-glycosidases untouched. Clean selectivity, which is exactly what you want in a probe that shouldn't cross-react.

original_title: Pulsed Electrolysis Unlocks Non-Noble-Metal Catalysis for Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substance Defluorination in Water
title: Breaking down PFAS with a pulsed current and no noble metal
blurb: A Co/Ni electrode defluorinates PFAS in water without the usual platinum-group catalyst, using pulsed rather than steady electrolysis to get around PFAS being repelled from the cathode. Co does the actual C–F bond activation and shuttles atomic hydrogen, while Ni just tunes Co's d-band center to make that work better. Cheaper catalyst chemistry, if it holds up past the beaker.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: From batch to flow: integrating in-line (deep) eutectic solvents with sequential downstream processing for sustainable biomass valorization
title: Deep eutectic solvents move from batch to flow for biomass processing
blurb: Same DES-based biomass valorization chemistry, just run in-line with the downstream separation steps instead of as a batch process. The pitch is a more continuous, scalable route rather than a new solvent chemistry.

original_title: Activity and Enantioselectivity of Hydroxynitrile Lyase from Granulicella tundricula: Computational Insights
title: DFT digs into why this Mn-dependent lyase picks one cyanohydrin enantiomer
blurb: GtHNL is a Mn(II) enzyme that makes R-cyanohydrins, with the aldehyde binding the metal's open coordination site and His106 acting as base. This computational study works out where the enantioselectivity actually comes from for benzaldehyde plus HCN, a mechanism question rather than a new catalyst.

original_title: Modular synthesis of benzothiophene-fused pentalenes reveals substituent-dependent antiaromaticity
title: A modular route to benzothiophene-fused pentalenes, tunable antiaromaticity included
blurb: Late-stage diversifiable synthesis of these fused pentalenes shows the antiaromatic character shifts with the substituent, turning what's usually a structural curiosity into something you can actually dial in for designing antiaromatic π-electron systems.

original_title: Near-infrared (NIR)-responsive activation of Ru-benziphthalocyanine complexes via singlet–triplet transition
title: Switching a Ru complex's aromaticity to control it with NIR light
blurb: Ru(II) π-arene complexes of benziphthalocyanine flip between 6π and 18π aromatic tautomers, and that switch is what governs whether near-IR light triggers photodissociation. Aromaticity as the on/off switch for the photophysics, not just a spectator property.

original_title: Harnessing Molecular Tautomerism to Tune Precursor Coordination Chemistry for Efficient and Stable Perovskite Solar Cells
title: Using purine's tautomers to steer perovskite crystallization
blurb: Purine sits in different tautomeric forms, each redistributing electron density across its nitrogens differently, and that's used here to tune how it coordinates Pb and hydrogen-bonds during perovskite film formation. The payoff claimed is more homogeneous crystallization and a more stable, better-performing cell, via picking the tautomer instead of a new additive.

original_title: Divergent assembly of fused polycyclic scaffolds from iodotriazole-tethered benzaldehydes
title: Iodotriazole aldehydes branch into a family of fused azaheterocycles
blurb: Pendant aldehydes on 5-iodo-1,2,3-triazoles cyclize into hemiaminals, then close with a transition-metal-free C(sp2)–N coupling to give diverse fused polycyclic scaffolds from one precursor class. No metal catalyst needed for the ring closure, which is the tidy part.

original_title: Regioisomerism‐Driven Microenvironment Modulation in Three‐Dimensional Covalent Organic Frameworks for Selective H 2 O 2 Photosynthesis
title: Same COF, just wired differently, and the photocatalysis changes
blurb: Two 3D covalent organic frameworks built from the same tetrathiafulvalene nodes and cyclooctatetrathiophene cores, but one links the thiophene units symmetrically (JUC-701) and one asymmetrically (JUC-702). Same composition, different internal charge distribution, and that's the lever they use to tune selective H2O2 photosynthesis rather than swapping in new building blocks.

original_title: Determination of reaction kinetics in three phase CO 2 methanation
title: Your CO2 methanation catalyst isn't fully wet, and the kinetics show it
blurb: In three-phase CO2 methanation the catalyst only partially wets, and they pull steady-state reaction kinetics out of that regime rather than assuming ideal contact.

original_title: Multi-Port Vacuum Assembly Device Designed for Simplified Point-of-Need Chemical and Biological Analyses Using Mass Spectrometry
title: One vacuum chamber, swap the ionization mode as needed
blurb: A proof-of-feasibility vacuum assembly with multiple accessible ports built to run different mass spec ionization techniques, including atmospheric-pressure methods, off the same rig. The pitch is point-of-need analysis without rebuilding the source for every sample type.

original_title: Recent advances in the synthesis of indolo[2,1- a ]isoquinolines from N -acryloyl indole derivatives
title: The state of the art in building indolo[2,1-a]isoquinolines
blurb: A review rounding up recent routes to indolo[2,1-a]isoquinoline scaffolds starting from N-acryloyl indole precursors.

original_title: Total syntheses of ent -aogacillin A and aogacillin B
title: Aogacillin B finally gets a total synthesis, seven steps
blurb: First asymmetric total syntheses of aogacillin B and ent-aogacillin A, both done in seven steps with a one-pot aldol/lactonization doing the heavy lifting.

original_title: Synthesis of carbazoles via aryl C–H activation triggered by surfactant-associated palladium nanoparticles under microwave-assisted heating
title: Carbazoles cooked up in water with soap and a microwave
blurb: Palladium nanoparticles get a activity boost from a micellar environment, enough to run C–H activation under microwave heating. The result is a Pd/DBU-catalyzed cyclization of 2-iodo-N-arylanilines into carbazoles in plain water with broad substrate scope.

original_title: Efficient and reversible boron coordination in a fluorescent BODIPY rotaxane
title: A BODIPY rotaxane you switch with Lewis acids instead of light
blurb: Thread a BODIPY through a biphenol-containing macrocycle and stopper it, then use BF3·OEt2 to knock the macrocycle off the boron center and AlCl3 to snap it back on, both swaps quantitative in about a minute. Both states still fluoresce at up to 91% quantum yield, and the threaded rotaxane shows better two-photon absorption than the unthreaded BODIPY.

original_title: Manganese N-Heterocyclic Carbene Complexes: Emerging Catalysts for Homogeneous Reduction Chemistry
title: Manganese NHC complexes angling for cheaper reduction catalysis
blurb: A review on manganese N-heterocyclic carbene complexes as the 3d-metal alternative to the usual late-transition-metal catalysts for homogeneous reductions.

original_title: Revealing the evolution of Cu II species and ammonia intermediates at different temperatures for selective catalytic reduction of NO over cost-effective Cu-exchanged zeolite X catalysts
title: A cheap zeolite that shows you where the ammonia actually sits
blurb: CuX-0.28, a cost-effective Cu-exchanged zeolite X, delivers strong low-temperature NO conversion and N2 selectivity. Modulation excitation spectroscopy catches NH3 preferentially parking on different Cu2+ sites depending on temperature, which is the mechanistic detail behind the performance.

original_title: Multicomponent domino synthesis of 6-azabicyclo[3.2.1]octanes and their cascade ring expansion toward 2-azabicyclo[4.3.1]decanes
title: A domino reaction that expands one azabicycle into a bigger one
blurb: A base-promoted, diastereoselective multicomponent domino reaction builds 6-azabicyclo[3.2.1]octanes using a new isoindole-based methylene unit, then cascades them through ring expansion into 2-azabicyclo[4.3.1]decanes.

original_title: Dual activation of CO 2 and N 2 facilitated by single Ta 4 + clusters
title: One Ta4+ cluster, two stubborn gases activated at once
blurb: A lone Ta4+ cluster reacts with CO2 and N2 side by side, and ELF/AdNDP bonding analysis pins the selectivity on local bonding and electron delocalization rather than anything about the metal alone. Gas-phase cluster chemistry, not a catalyst on a shelf, but a clean mechanistic read on why one activates faster than the other.

original_title: "CO2 Hydrogenation to Ethanol and Higher Hydrocarbons over K-Promoted LaCuxFe1–xO3: An Integrated Experimental and CFD Study"
title: K-promoted LaCuFeO3 pushes CO2 hydrogenation past methanol
blurb: Pairs actual runs with CFD modeling of a K-promoted LaCuxFe1-xO3 perovskite that hydrogenates CO2 to ethanol and other C2+ products instead of stalling at methanol. Getting past the C1 wall is the part that usually doesn't work, so that's the news here.

original_title: Greening water-lean solvents for CO 2 capture: replacing toxic 1-methyl-2-pyrrolidone with high-performance eco-friendly cosolvents
title: Swapping the reprotoxic NMP out of CO2 capture solvents
blurb: Large-scale screening finds eco-friendly cosolvents that replace NMP, a known reprotoxin, in water-lean CO2 capture systems, with better capture performance and lower energy cost. The kind of unglamorous solvent-swap work that actually matters if this stuff gets built at scale.

original_title: Trans-Influence-Driven Coordination Plasticity in Carbazolide NNN Pincer Nickel(II) Complexes
title: A pincer ligand with a strong enough trans influence to reshape the whole complex
blurb: Carbazolide NNN pincer ligands push such a strong trans influence on nickel(II) that the coordination geometry itself shifts with the ancillary ligand: halides go octahedral and partially ionize the Ni-X bond in coordinating solvents, while oxygen donors instead build mu-alkoxide dimers. Trans influence actually doing structural work, not just showing up as an NMR shift.

original_title: Outcomes of [(177)Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 radioligand therapy with and without concurrent enzalutamide in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer: a single-center retrospective study.
title: Adding enzalutamide alongside Lu-177-PSMA-617, does it help
blurb: Single-center retrospective comparing outcomes for Lu-177-PSMA-617 given with versus without concurrent enzalutamide in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Retrospective and single-site, so treat it as a lead toward a real combination trial rather than an answer.
venue: Eur J Nucl Med Mol Imaging

original_title: Multifunctional Double-Network Hydrogel Synergistically Enhanced by Zirconium Ions and Carbon Quantum Dots.
title: Zirconium ions and carbon quantum dots team up in a double-network hydrogel
blurb: A double-network hydrogel with its properties boosted by zirconium ions and carbon quantum dots working together rather than either additive alone.

original_title: Deuterated Aprotic Electrolytes Enable Rechargeable Lithium Batteries With High (Electro)Chemical and Thermal Stability
title: Swap the C-H for C-D and the electrolyte stops eating itself
blurb: Deuterating the polarizable C-H sites in aprotic ether and ester battery electrolytes slows the proton-transfer side reactions that decompose them at high-voltage cathodes, via a straightforward kinetic isotope effect. Reported payoff is better electrochemical and thermal stability in a rechargeable lithium cell, for the cost of deuterated solvent.

original_title: Single crystal covalent organic frameworks
title: Getting covalent organic frameworks to actually grow as single crystals
blurb: A review rounding up strategies for making single-crystal COFs rather than the usual polycrystalline powders, and tying that crystallization control to which structural and functional properties actually hold up. No new data, just the state of the field.

original_title: Electrostatic preactivation of dioxygen without metal redox activity
title: O2 won't react because its own electron acceptor doesn't exist yet
blurb: Beyond the usual spin-restriction and first-electron-cost excuses for why O2 is so sluggish, this points out a third problem: at O2's resting geometry, the anion that's supposed to grab the incoming electron isn't even bound, so there's nothing there to accept it. Reframes activation around the electrostatic surroundings shaping that acceptor into existence, rather than needing a metal to do redox chemistry on it.
